name: CC Overstay Fines — generated v1
description: CC Overstay Fines (road-map #31). Scheduled monthly, 15th 06:00 Asia/Dubai, over the previous full calendar month. Threshold AED 200 strict >, a TRIGGER not a deductible, recovered onto the MAID'S LOAN. Expense 1589. DRAFT - never publish.

main.node: Get CC Change of Status Transactions

nodes.name: Build Run Context
nodes.notes: The check page answers "How is it triggered? — Manual only", so there is no webhook, no shared secret and no callback allowlist to inherit wrong. Every constant downstream is read from here and every one of them is CC's: threshold 200 strict >, base 575.65, expense 1589. MV Overstay Fines is 300 recovered from the CLIENT on expense 1677 and the two share a workbook.

nodes.name: Get CC Change of Status Transactions
nodes.notes: THE COHORT — built from the cc_change_of_status_transaction ERP Variables row, not from any sibling flow. Operation "=" not "like", pagecode ManageTransactions, Bearer. MEASURED 2026-08-12 over nine months: 963 rows, every month content.length == totalElements, every row expense.id 1589. The CC expense is 1589; the MV one is 1677 and the names differ by three characters.

nodes.name: Build Error Callback
nodes.notes: Status-code-first classification, deduped across parallel failures. Reached from every ERP node's error output and from the Error Trigger.

nodes.name: Verify Cohort Pull
nodes.notes: OWNS THE POPULATION PROOF. Three separate obligations: the walk must reconcile to totalElements, an empty result ABORTS (a month with zero CC change-of-status transactions is a broken query, never "no findings"), and no foreign expense.id may appear. Build Run Row reads the proof from THIS node by name — on the MV build it arrived as {} because an intermediate node dropped it, so every run stamped itself untrustworthy.

nodes.name: Split Transactions
nodes.notes: Intake gates 1 and 2 — filtering happens at INTAKE, not at scoring, and the excluded counts are published so "out of scope" is never reported as "clean". Sets pairedItem itself: n8n only auto-pairs Run-Once-for-EACH-Item nodes. Emits a sentinel when the month carries no over-base row at all — measured live, May and June 2026 both did, and emitting nothing would strand the whole delivery band and write no Runs row.

nodes.name: Has Cases?
nodes.notes: Routes the empty-month sentinel around the enrichment lane so it can never be interpolated into a URL path, while keeping the run alive all the way to the Runs row.

nodes.name: Merge Streams
nodes.notes: Input 0 = the enriched lane. Input 1 = unattributed records and the empty-month sentinel. Both must reach scoring: an unattributed record is a review case, not a disappearance.

nodes.name: Attach Identity
nodes.notes: Gate 3. maid = housemaids[0].housemaid.id and nothing else. Never resolved from the transaction description even though it contains her name, and never joined to a fine or a loan by amount, date or name. contractId comes back EMPTY on CC transactions — there is no contract to scope to, identity is the maid.

nodes.name: Identity Resolved?
nodes.notes: The URL-path guard. An unattributed record leaves the lane BEFORE an empty id can be interpolated into a path — which makes ERP answer 400 on the path segment and kills the run. It still publishes as review.

nodes.name: Get Overstay Fines
nodes.notes: Returns a BARE JSON ARRAY, so fullResponse is ON. Without it n8n splits the array into one item per element: a maid with ZERO fines produces ZERO items and disappears from the run, a maid with two produces two, and every downstream pairing shifts. That exact defect made all 30 MV cases come out fines_unreadable. pagecode VisaProcessingPage is load-bearing.

nodes.name: Attach Fines
nodes.notes: Normalises only. Skips placeholder rows (net AND days both 0 — 30 of 65 live over-base transactions had nothing else). Excludes MV maids on housemaidType = MaidVisa, which fires for real: five fine rows inside the CC 1589 population read MaidVisa live. reductionReason is documented as an object {id,label} and arrives as a plain empty STRING on all 67 live CC rows — both shapes are handled. phoneNumber is dropped.

nodes.name: Get Housemaid Loans
nodes.notes: The recovery. A CC maid repays her overstay fine through a loan on her profile, not through a client payment — there is no contract to scope a payment search to. Also a BARE JSON ARRAY (checked, not assumed: 83 loans across 64 maids read live), so fullResponse is ON here too.

nodes.name: Attach Loans
nodes.notes: Gate 8. Sums `amount` (principal) across OVERSTAY_FINES_FEES loans. Never remainingAmount — repayments shrink it to zero and a correctly loaded loan then reads as never added. Never gates on status: it came back an EMPTY STRING on loan 80186, a correct case. waivedAmount 0.0 is the NORMAL unwaived value — all 27 read live carried it.

nodes.name: Compute Case States
nodes.notes: The ELEVEN deterministic gates in the policy page's order. Gate 7 (the fine-side waiver) is read BEFORE any comparison so a missing-loan finding can never be raised over a waived fine — on the MV side that mechanism accounted for 19 of 20 reported findings. NO gap tolerance: this check declares none and none is borrowed. 200 is a TRIGGER, not a deductible — above it the WHOLE fine goes on her loan.

nodes.name: Select Verifier Cases
nodes.notes: Only cases the gates could NOT settle: a waived loan (gate 9) or a fine reduction whose reason does not settle it (verifier rule 2). Everything else is arithmetic and stays arithmetic. Emits a sentinel when nothing needs judging — the normal outcome — so the sync barrier and everything after it still run.

nodes.name: Get Maid Complaints
nodes.notes: The maid's own To-do list — the CC counterpart of reading the CLIENT's complaints on MV, because here the debt sits on the maid. NEVER filtered by complaintType: not one live type is overstay-related and on CC Maids Salary Raise the relevant To-dos spanned seven type labels. size=200 in ONE call: the documented "caps at 40 on page 0" is the DEFAULT PAGE SIZE, not a server cap — measured on twelve maids 2026-08-12, maid 113572 returned all 74 rows with content.length == totalElements. The next node asserts that equality rather than assuming it.

nodes.name: Join Verdict Paths
nodes.notes: Sync barrier over three paths: the model, the preset, and the no-verifier-cases sentinel. Without it each fires Merge Agent Verdicts separately and the run writes its tables more than once.

nodes.name: Split Relevant Complaints
nodes.notes: Keeps initialDescription in full — a primary staff-written source already on the list response. DROPS ERP's summary and recentSummary entirely so no verdict can rest on ERP's own compression. The keyword scan decides which threads are worth a CALL and is never itself evidence. Asserts one response item per verifier case before using index alignment.

nodes.name: Get Complaint Thread
nodes.notes: The REAL comment thread — what staff actually typed. With initialDescription this is the whole of the evidence this check allows. content[].text is HTML and is stripped in the next node before the model ever sees it.

nodes.name: Attach Threads to Cases
nodes.notes: Folds threads back per case and strips the HTML. A missing thread shows as an EMPTY ARRAY, never as "no complaint" — the two are different claims and only one is evidence.

nodes.name: Build Evidence Bundle
nodes.notes: Pre-computes the arithmetic so the model cannot invent a different expectation, and settles two shapes in code: no staff text anywhere, and a complaint list that came back incomplete. Neither preset ever CLEARS a case.

options.systemMessage:
You are the verifier for the maids.cc audit "CC Overstay Fines" (road-map #31).

WHAT THIS CHECK IS ABOUT
We paid a CC maid's overstay fine. Above AED 200 the WHOLE fine is supposed to go
onto her loan and be recovered from her. Sometimes a loan was added and then
written off, or the fine itself was reduced. The numbers say only HOW MUCH was
written off. Only the note beside them says whether that was AUTHORISED. Deciding
that, and nothing wider, is your entire job.

YOU ARE NOT ASKED TO DO ARITHMETIC. Every amount, threshold and comparison has
already been computed and is given to you as fact. Never recompute an expectation,
never dispute a figure, never decide whether a loan exists.

THE THREE VERDICTS — return one, EXACTLY as written, never paraphrased:
  "All is good - waiver justified"        the record states WHY the write-off was allowed
  "Written off without justification"     something was waived and nothing says why
  "Awaiting accounting decision"          not settled, and not a finding either

TEN HARD STOPS. Each one is a "Never" line from the audit's own policy page.

 1. Never accept a KEYWORD MATCH as the justification. A note containing the word
    "waived" or "approved" is not a justification. Quote the sentence that
    authorises it, or do not clear the case.

 2. Never accept the EXISTENCE of a note as the justification. A note saying WHAT
    was done is not a note saying WHY it was allowed. The waive note is written by
    a machine in the form
      "<amount> AED were waived by <Name> on <DD/MM/YYYY> because <reason>"
    Who and when are always there and are never, by themselves, a justification.
    Only the text after "because" can be one, and only if it states a ground.

 3. Never treat a BLANK reason as clean. Absence of a reason is not a reason. This
    is the single path by which money is absorbed without anyone deciding to
    absorb it, and it is the exact thing this check exists to surface.

 4. Never infer the justification from the amount, the date, or who created the
    loan. Seniority is not authorisation.

 5. Never rely on ERP's auto-generated `summary` or `recentSummary`. They are not
    given to you. Your evidence is what staff actually wrote: the loan's
    waiveNotes, the fine's reductionReason, and the maid's complaints —
    initialDescription plus the real comment thread.

 6. Never report "explained" without the QUOTE. A label with nothing behind it is
    an assertion, not evidence. Every clearance carries the verbatim sentence it
    rests on, copied exactly, and the link it came from.

 7. Never read ZERO COMPLAINTS as a clearance. A maid with no complaints is
    evidence of nothing either way; the verdict then rests on the waiver fields
    alone.

 8. Never clear a case whose complaint list is marked INCOMPLETE on the strength of
    what is absent. If the justification could have been in the rows we could not
    read, the verdict is "Awaiting accounting decision", never a clearance.

 9. Never judge whether the waiver was a GOOD commercial decision. You judge only
    whether the record justifies it. A badly-reasoned but clearly-stated and
    authorised ground is a clearance.

10. Never invent, paraphrase, translate, tidy or complete a quote. Copy it
    character for character from the evidence you were given. If no quote in the
    evidence supports the verdict, the verdict is not a clearance.

PRIVACY. Only your verdict and the quoted justification leave this check. Never
copy a phone number, an address, a salary or a bank detail into any field, even if
it appears inside a sentence you would otherwise quote — cut the sentence short
instead.

CONFIDENCE. "high" only when a single quoted sentence settles it on its own.
"medium" when it takes reading several pieces together. "low" when you are
choosing between readings — and a low-confidence clearance is not a clearance,
it is "Awaiting accounting decision".

nodes.name: Verify Waivers
nodes.notes: Judges ONE question: does the record say WHY the write-off was allowed. Amounts, thresholds and whether a loan exists at all stay deterministic and are handed over as facts.

nodes.name: Verdict Schema
nodes.notes: Constrains the model to the THREE allowed verdicts and forces a verbatim quote plus the link it came from. Without it the agent returns free prose and a clearance with nothing behind it.

nodes.name: Merge Agent Verdicts
nodes.notes: Produces the FINAL state per case. This runs BEFORE the payload, the summary and all three table writes — on the MV build the verifier sat after them, so the Cases table permanently held the pre-AI verdict and the run summary called itself provisional. Also enforces rule 6 in code: a clearance without a quoted sentence that states WHY is downgraded automatically.

nodes.name: Adjudicate Cases
nodes.notes: Never re-derives an expectation. Assembles the report lines the check page asks for, with reds SPLIT between "never loaned" and "written off without justification" so the two are not read as one failure. Outstanding money counts only billable reds; a surplus never offsets a gap.

nodes.name: Build Case Rows
nodes.notes: NULL IS NOT ZERO: where there is no authoritative amount the numeric key is OMITTED, never written as 0. Emits a marker row rather than nothing when the month scored no case.

nodes.name: Build Verdict Rows
nodes.notes: EVERY column this writes has a producer in this file. The MV build created a Verdicts table and referenced it from no node at all, and shipped a recovery_followup column nothing anywhere writes. Joined to Cases on case_key.

nodes.name: Build Run Row
nodes.notes: Reads the population proof straight from Verify Cohort Pull, the node that OWNS it — not from whatever survived three transforms. Counts, totals and flags only; no per-maid amount reaches this row.

nodes.name: Build Case Payload
nodes.notes: The portal envelope: counts, totals and flags, plus the verifier verdict and its quote. Per-maid amounts stay in the Cases table and the workbook. Wired AFTER the three durable writes so a failing callback cannot cost them.

nodes.name: Portal Delivery Declared?
nodes.notes: Reads the declaration; it does not switch it. A declared target is never reachable ONLY through another target — this gate sits on its own branch and gates nothing but the callback.

nodes.name: Format Review Email
nodes.notes: Its OWN branch off Adjudicate Cases, never chained behind the portal callback. On the MV build this email sat downstream of a callback gated on portal === true while the runner declared portal:false, so it never fired once.

nodes.name: Draft: cases to review
nodes.notes: DISABLED and a DRAFT, with no credential attached. The check page answers Email = no, and guessing a Gmail credential risks sending as a colleague. The node that builds its content still runs, so the day the answer changes the content is already tested.

nodes.name: Build Error Run Row
nodes.notes: A failed run gets a Runs row too — overall: error, the error code, zeroed counts. Wired FIRST in the rail so the durable write cannot be lost to a later failing step. Without it the runs log silently omits exactly the runs a reader most needs.

nodes.name: Draft: audit failed
nodes.notes: DISABLED and a DRAFT, no credential.

parameters.content:
## 1 · Intake — one door
**Manual only**, per the check page. There is no webhook, so there is no shared secret and no callback allowlist to inherit from a different check — which is the open gap the MV build had to report.

Every constant lives in `Build Run Context` and every one is **CC's**: threshold **200** strict `>`, base **575.65**, expense **1589**. MV is 300, the CLIENT pays, expense 1677. The two checks share one workbook and that is exactly how a shared constant gets in.

## 2 · Cohort
`POST /accounting/transactions/page/advancesearch` — the **legacy** route, not `advancesearchNew`. pagecode **ManageTransactions**, filter `expense.id` **=** **1589**, window `between` on `date`.

**Why the legacy route (2026-08-30).** Only this one projects the `housemaids` link, so identity arrives WITH the population. `Get Transaction Detail` — one ERP call per over-base transaction, purely to learn the maid — is deleted, and the budget gate drops from 3 calls per transaction to 2. The two routes return rows that look identical in every field this flow reads EXCEPT `housemaids`, so `Verify Cohort Pull` gate (d) aborts the run if not one row carries attribution. Do not repoint this URL.

**Filter is `expense.id`, not `expense.name`.** The searchable `expense.name` and the projected one are different strings on this endpoint — a name that reads back off a live row can match zero rows. Verified equivalent before the swap: 1084 = 1084 all-time, 694 = 694 for Apr–Aug 2026.

MEASURED 2026-08-12 across **nine months / 963 transactions**: every month `content.length == totalElements`, every row expense.id 1589. Dec 2025 10 · Jan 229 · Feb 93 · Mar 58 · Apr 53 · May 142 · Jun 274 · Jul 58 · Aug 46.

MEASURED 2026-08-30 on 200 live cohort rows: **200 of 200 carried attribution**, 0 multi-maid, `contractId` empty on 199.

⚠️ The check page says August is "46 transactions, 4 above base". The walk finds **6** above base — the page measured page 0 of 40 only.

May and June carried **zero** over-base rows, so the empty-case path is real and is handled by the sentinel, not by stranding the run.

## 3 · Enrichment — PACED, and the number is the policy's
Three calls per over-base transaction: detail → overstay fines → **loans** (CC recovers from the maid, not the client; `contractId` is empty on CC transactions).

All at **batchSize 2 / batchInterval 500 ms** — `ERP-LOAD-POLICY.md` §1, 4 req/s. Until 2026-08-23 this note said **5 / 500**, which is 10 req/s, and the nodes agreed with it. A number in prose that contradicts the ceiling is worse than no note: it reads as a decision and stops the next reader looking.

**Why 2 and not 4-at-1000.** Both are 4 req/s; the first holds two connections open, the second four. When the rate is identical, take the lower peak — it is free.

Each fan-out is followed by its own **`Judge … Batch`** node carrying the §5 circuit breaker. Those three HTTP nodes are on **continueRegularOutput on purpose**: a failure has to arrive at the breaker as an item to be counted. Routed out of the error output it would reach the lease rail and be counted by nobody.

**Both array endpoints set `fullResponse: true`.** n8n splits a bare top-level array into one item per element: without it a maid with zero fines produces zero items and vanishes, and a maid with two shifts every downstream pairing. That defect made all 30 MV cases read `fines_unreadable`.

## 4 · Verifier — BEFORE the tables, not after
Jacky's explicit instruction. On MV the verifier ran in a late band after the results callback and after `Write Cases`, so the Cases table permanently held the pre-AI verdict, the run summary called itself "provisional", and nothing ever corrected either.

Here it runs first, so Cases and Runs carry **final** states and correct red/green counts in one pass.

Only unsettled cases reach the model: a waived loan, or a fine reduction whose reason does not settle it. **Zero live cases in nine months** — so this band is wired and tested offline but has never run against a real waiver. The `waiveNotes` TEMPLATE is verified from three real waived loans of other types on the same endpoint.

## 5 · Delivery — five independent branches
Each declared target hangs off `Adjudicate Cases` directly. **Durable writes come first in connection order**, so a failing callback cannot cost the record.

1 `Write Cases` · 2 `Write Verdicts` · 3 `Write Run` · 4 portal callback (gated, declared **off**) · 5 review email (draft, disabled).

On MV the entire post-verifier band sat behind `delivery.portal === true` while the runner declared `portal:false`, so every AI verdict was discarded and the email — chained *behind* the callback — never fired.

## Error rail — record, release, THEN fail
Every single-output node between `Acquire ERP Lease` and `Release ERP Lease` routes its error output to `Build Error Callback`. The Error Trigger reaches it too, but that path is decoration here: **this check is manual-only and n8n does not fire error workflows for manual executions.**

Then, in order:
1 **Runs row** (`overall: error`, zeroed counts, whatever the population proof reached) · 2 portal callback (disabled) · 3 failure draft · 4 **`Release Lease (error)`** · 5 **`Fail Loudly`**.

**The capture comes first on purpose.** An Execute Sub-workflow node replaces the item it is given with the sub-workflow's return value, so anything reading the failure has to read it *before* the lease release runs.

**`Fail Loudly` re-throws.** n8n marks an execution SUCCESS when it runs off the end of an error output. A rail that released the lease and stopped would turn a failed audit into one the run log calls fine — worse than the stranded lease it fixes, because a stranded lease is loud within three hours and a silently-successful audit is never looked at again.

**Named blind spots**, left unwired because their error output is not at an index worth guessing: `Has Cases?`, `Identity Resolved?`, `Any Verifier Cases?`, `Needs the model?`, `Portal Delivery Declared?`, `Merge Streams`, `Join Verdict Paths`, `Verify Waivers`. If one of those kills the run, nothing releases the lease and the 3-hour staleness rule cleans up.

nodes.name: Fail Loudly
nodes.notes: The end of the error rail, replacing Fail The Run. It re-throws: n8n marks an execution SUCCESS when it runs off the end of an error output, so a rail that released the lease and stopped would turn a failed audit into one the run log reports as fine - worse than the stranded lease it fixes, because a stranded lease is loud within three hours and a silently-successful audit is never looked at again.

nodes.name: ERP Budget Gate
nodes.notes: ERP-LOAD-POLICY.md §3. Projects the whole run's ERP cost before the first per-entity call and THROWS if it exceeds params.erp_call_budget (set in Build Run Context, default 2000). It never trims the cohort: a partial audit that looks complete is the failure this check family exists to prevent.

nodes.name: Judge Fines Batch
nodes.notes: ERP-LOAD-POLICY.md §5. Judges the overstay-fines batch and passes it on unchanged. Generated by tools/make_breaker_block.py - do not hand-edit.

nodes.name: Judge Loans Batch
nodes.notes: ERP-LOAD-POLICY.md §5. Judges the housemaid-loans batch and passes it on unchanged. Generated by tools/make_breaker_block.py - do not hand-edit.

nodes.name: Judge Complaints Batch
nodes.notes: ERP-LOAD-POLICY.md §5. Judges the maid-complaints batch and passes it on unchanged. Generated by tools/make_breaker_block.py - do not hand-edit.

nodes.name: Judge Threads Batch
nodes.notes: ERP-LOAD-POLICY.md §5. Judges the complaint-thread batch and passes it on unchanged. Generated by tools/make_breaker_block.py - do not hand-edit.

parameters.content:
## 0 · ERP load policy — the four layers
`../ERP-LOAD-POLICY.md`, brought in 2026-08-23. Each layer sees exactly one thing and is blind to the others; drop one and the rest do not cover for it.

**§4 lease** — `Acquire ERP Lease` before the cohort walk, `Release ERP Lease` at the **last ERP call**, `Release Lease (error)` on the rail. Knows who *else* is calling ERP and nothing else.
The success release is a **dead-end parallel branch** off two points that between them cover every path: `Judge Threads Batch` (after `Get Complaint Thread`) and `Any Verifier Cases?` **output 1** (the no-verifier sentinel, after `Get Housemaid Loans`). Exactly one fires per run.
Until 2026-08-24 it hung off `Write Run`, at the end of the delivery tail. **A node that returns zero items does not fail** — it stops its branch and every node after it is never executed, while n8n still reports the run as a **success** — so any empty tail node silently deleted the release and the next audit queued behind a holder that had already exited.

**§1 pacing** — 2 in flight / 500 ms on every per-item node; the cohort pager at 1 / 500 ms with `requestInterval` 500 and `maxRequests` 50. Knows the rate and nothing about the count.

**§3 budget gate** — `ERP Budget Gate`, before the first per-entity call. Projects sweep pages + 3/transaction + the verifier band at its measured worst case (1 list + up to 74 threads) and **throws**. It never trims the cohort: a partial audit that looks complete is the failure this family exists to prevent. Budget: `params.erp_call_budget` in `Build Run Context`, default 2000.

**§5 breakers** — `Judge Detail / Fines / Loans / Complaints / Threads Batch`. Know how ERP is *answering* and nothing about who else is calling. Each says in its own header which of the three thresholds can actually fire; **latency can fire in none of them**, because every fan-out here runs once per run and there is no earlier batch of the same key to baseline against.

nodes.name: Run Monthly
nodes.notes: Monthly on the 15th at 06:00 Asia/Dubai, auditing the previous full calendar month. The two-week lag is deliberate - payments need time to settle. Feeds the same Build Run Context node as the manual trigger, so both entries share one source of truth and one window rule. NOTE: this cannot succeed until the flow's ERP credential holds a PRODUCTION token - the staging credential is dated and ERP tokens last 24h.
